summary: Built and ran a reusable exact certificate constructor/validator for the corrected amplifier (checks/amp_cert.py, one process, exact Fractions, no solver, no search). It works in Q(sqrt p, sqrt m) with basis (1, sqrt p, sqrt m, sqrt(pm)), builds the chain and rotated chain, enumerates ALL induced unit edges, checks distinctness and the counts, verifies the final endpoint distance exactly, and decides non-k-colourability by bounded exhaustive enumeration. Three instances pass: k=2 path gadget n=3 (D=3/4, |X|=13=bound, 13 induced edges, 13/13 generating, final edge unit, 0 of 2^13 proper 2-colourings, field Q(sqrt7,sqrt5), cos=1/9, sin=(4/9)sqrt5); k=2 path n=2 giving D=1/2 exactly with theta=pi (|X|=9, 9 edges, 0 of 2^9 colourings) - the promised boundary case works; k=3 diamond n=1 (the Moser spindle: |X|=7, 11 induced edges = 11 generating, 0 of 3^7 proper 3-colourings, Q(sqrt3,sqrt11), cos=5/6, sin=(1/6)sqrt11). In all three |X| attains the bound, so no unintended overlaps, and induced = generating, so no accidental edges; both are verified, not assumed. Corrected three prose points: equality in the vertex bound requires precisely the intended overlaps including the n-1 consecutive identifications; other gadget vertices are not constrained by (H2) and need not differ from the anchors; and the claim is now 'no forcing pair at the target k', since k=2 and k=3 forcing pairs are known, while Heule553 is pair-separating at k>=5 and cannot be the input.
verified_results: GRADE [A] Instance k2-path-n3: gadget = path p-r-q with p=(0,0), r=(1/8,(3/8)sqrt7), q=(1/4,0), edges {p-r, r-q} (both unit, exact), ||v||^2 = 1/16 in Q, n = 3, D = 3/4, cos theta = 1/9, sin theta = (4/9)sqrt5 in Q(sqrt7,sqrt5). Point set: 13 distinct points attaining the bound 2nV-2n+1 = 13; 13 induced unit edges; 13 distinct generating edges out of 13 entries, all verified unit; final endpoint pair at squared distance exactly 1 and distinct; exhaustive check of all 2^13 2-colourings finds zero proper ones.

GRADE [A] Instance k2-path-n2-D-half (the D = 1/2 boundary): same gadget, n = 2 so D = 1/2 exactly, theta = pi (cos = -1, sin = 0, no field extension needed beyond Q(sqrt7)). 9 distinct points = the bound 2nV-2n+1 = 9; 9 induced edges = 9 generating entries; final endpoints -(1/2,0) and (1/2,0) at distance exactly 1 and distinct; zero proper 2-colourings among all 2^9. This confirms that the antipodal boundary case is admissible and produces a genuine odd cycle rather than a degenerate or coincident configuration.

GRADE [A] Instance k3-diamond-n1: diamond with base (0,0)-(1,0) and tips (1/2,+-sqrt3/2); p, q the tips, ||v||^2 = 3, n = 1, D = sqrt3, cos theta = 5/6, sin theta = (1/6)sqrt11 in Q(sqrt3,sqrt11). 7 distinct points = the bound; 11 induced unit edges = 11 generating entries (the Moser spindle); final edge unit; zero proper 3-colourings among all 3^7. This is the positive control reproducing the record's exact spindle in the record's own field.

GRADE [P] Prose corrections in AMPLIFIER.md: (i) equality in |C_n| <= nV-(n-1) requires precisely the intended overlaps - the n-1 consecutive identifications q+jv = p+(j+1)v and the single shared point 0 - and no others; (ii) the copy's other V-2 points are not constrained by (H2) and in general need not differ in colour from the anchors, so 'carry the other colours' was too strong; (iii) the correct scope statement is that no forcing pair at the target k is known, while k=2 and k=3 forcing pairs are known and are exactly the positive controls used, and Heule553 is certified pair-separating at k >= 5, the opposite of (H2), so it cannot be the input.

GRADE [A] Validator design: the field is Q(sqrt p, sqrt m) with Fraction coefficients and basis (1, sqrt p, sqrt m, sqrt(pm)); the rotation coefficients are cos theta = 1 - 1/(2D^2) and sin theta = (t/(2D^2))sqrt(m) where 4D^2-1 = m t^2 with m squarefree, computed from a squarefree decomposition of a rational; only ||v||^2 is used, never ||v||, so no spurious field extension is introduced. Duplicate points are merged by exact coefficient equality, so distinctness is exact rather than numerical.
conjectures: The validator is the right asset to hand to any chat that produces a candidate gadget: given exact coordinates, a k-colouring of the gadget and a proof of (H2), it determines n from the exact test 4n^2||v||^2 >= 1, builds the point set, and reports the true counts and the induced edge list - so the 'no accidental edges' question becomes a computation rather than an assumption.

In all three tested instances accidental edges and unintended overlaps happen to be absent; whether that persists for larger n or other gadgets is unknown and must not be assumed, which is why the theorem is stated only as a lower bound.

The D = 1/2 case being non-degenerate suggests the amplifier can be used at exactly the threshold, which matters for a gadget whose forced-pair distance is small: n = ceil(1/(2||v||)) is enough, with no strictness slack needed.
tests_run: One computation, one process, exact Fractions, no solver and no search beyond bounded enumeration: python3 checks/amp_cert.py -> exit 0 in about 0.03 s, well inside the 60 s budget. It builds and validates the three instances, prints the per-instance summary (counts, final-edge unit test, number of proper k-colourings) and writes amp_certificates.json with exact coordinates, generating-edge lists, full induced-edge lists and all check results.
failed_routes: Two defects in my first draft of the validator were found and fixed before any result was reported (a squarefree-decomposition slip that put the leftover numerator prime into t, and a gadget coordinate placed in the sqrt(m) slot instead of the sqrt(p) slot); the corrected run is the only one recorded.

Not attempted, by instruction: any search for k = 5 or k = 6 forcing pairs; any solver or Lean; any change to the theorem to avoid coincidences (accidental edges remain allowed and are reported by the validator rather than excluded).
next_step: Hold as an asset. If a candidate gadget appears, feed its exact coordinates and (H2) proof to checks/amp_cert.py: it will fix n by the exact test 2n||v|| >= 1, emit the point set, the true induced edge list and the counts, and verify the final unit edge, so that the only remaining obligation is (H2) itself.
